mainTopic: Two lengths of תוך כדי דיבור in רבי יוסי's view, and רבא's rule that הכחשה is the beginning of הזמה, which אביי disputes.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation from the previous amud. רבי and רבי יוסי argue about testimony that is partly refuted, and their argument depends on whether words said right after a statement (תוך כדי דיבור) count as part of it. The גמרא challenges this from a משנה in תמורה. There, רבי יוסי says that someone who changes his mind within תוך כדי דיבור cannot undo his first label. The answer is that there are two lengths of תוך כדי דיבור: the time of a student's long greeting to his רב, and the time of a רב's short greeting to his student. רבי יוסי counts only the shorter one. Next, רבא rules that witnesses who were first contradicted and later made זוממין still get the punishment of זוממין, because הכחשה is the beginning of הזמה. He proves it from a ברייתא about witnesses testifying on a master who blinded his slave's eye and knocked out his tooth, reading it as a case with three sets of witnesses. אביי rejects the proof by reading the ברייתא as a case with only two sets of witnesses. He then begins to show why his reading is right, and that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute depends on תוך כדי דיבור
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that something said right after an earlier statement does not join it. רבי יוסי holds that it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי holds that a statement made within the short time it takes to speak] is not like one continuous statement. רבי יוסי holds that a statement made within that time is like one continuous statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its explanation of what רבי and רבי יוסי argue about. Their argument depends on the rule of תוך כדי דיבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the second testimony is separate from the first. So when part of it is refuted, the other part still stands. For רבי יוסי, words said right after each other count as one testimony, so refuting part of it knocks out all of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Within the short moment it takes to speak a brief phrase.
Counts as part of the same statement.
Holds, is of the opinion.

phrases.english: is not like one continuous statement,
and Rabbi Yosei holds:
within the time of speaking is like continuous speech.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the רבי / רבי יוסי dispute, which began before this text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the underlying principle behind the dispute
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי: תוך כדי דיבור is not like speech. רבי יוסי: it is like speech.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה in תמורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יוסי really holds this. It quotes a משנה about someone who names an animal as a substitute for two different offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי really hold that a statement made within the time of speaking is like continuous speech? But we learned in a משנה: if someone says 'This is a substitute for an עולה, a substitute for a שלמים', it is a substitute for an עולה. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to challenge the idea that רבי יוסי holds תוך כדי דיבור כדיבור דמי. Here it begins quoting a משנה from מסכת תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, a person says two labels one right after the other. According to רבי מאיר, only the first label counts. The challenge itself will come from רבי יוסי's opinion in the next part of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal someone tries to swap in for a קרבן. It becomes holy too.
A burnt-offering, burned completely on the מזבח.
A peace-offering, which its owners mostly eat.

phrases.english: But does Rabbi Yosei hold
that within the time of speaking is like continuous speech?
But didn't we learn in a Mishnah:
"This is a substitute for a burnt-offering, a substitute for a peace-offering" –
it is a substitute for a burnt-offering,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the position just given to רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי holds תוך כדי דיבור כדיבור דמי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about two labels said one after the other may show that רבי יוסי does not treat the second label as joined to the first.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's view in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says both labels count if he meant both from the start. But if he changed his mind and then said 'שלמים', it is an עולה substitute.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: if this is what he intended from the start, his words stand, since it is impossible to say two names at once. But if he said 'a substitute for an עולה' and then changed his mind and said 'a substitute for a שלמים', it is a substitute for an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the משנה. This part, רבי יוסי's opinion, is the source of the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי gives two cases. If the person planned both labels from the start, both count, because nobody can say two words at the same moment. If he changed his mind after the first label, the second label does not take effect. That seems to show the later words do not undo or join what he said first.

keyTerms.meaning: He intended it from the beginning.

keyTerms.term: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִקְרוֹת שְׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת כְּאֶחָד
keyTerms.meaning: It is impossible to say two names at once.
His words stand, they take effect.
He changed his mind, reconsidered.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In the first he meant both labels all along, so both count. In the second he changed his mind midway, so only the first label counts.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
If he intended this from the start,
phrases.notes: "This" means that the animal should be a substitute for both offerings.

phrases.english: since it is impossible
to call it by two names at once –
his words stand.
But if he said: "A substitute for a burnt-offering,"
and changed his mind and said: "A substitute for a peace-offering" –
it is a substitute for a burnt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted משנה with רבי יוסי's opinion, the part the challenge rests on.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's supposed view that תוך כדי דיבור כדיבור דמי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here a second statement made after changing his mind does not change the first. This seems to go against treating words said right afterward as part of the first statement.

steps.title: Why state the obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier discussion that asked why רבי יוסי needed to rule on 'נמלך'. It seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed this: if he changed his mind, that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up an earlier discussion of this משנה, which asked why the 'changed his mind' case needed to be taught. This is setting up the next move, which will show what 'נמלך' really means here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone already gave the animal one status and later changes his mind, of course he cannot undo it. So רבי יוסי's ruling seems unnecessary. This question will push the גמרא to read the case in a sharper way, and that reading is what makes it a real challenge to step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it. This recalls an earlier discussion in the בית מדרש.
Obvious! This asks why something so clear needed to be said.

steps.whyThisMatters: This question is the key to the challenge. The answer will show which kind of changing one's mind רבי יוסי meant, and that will show his view on תוך כדי דיבור.

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
If he changed his mind, it is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the last clause of רבי יוסי's ruling to sharpen the challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוסי needed to teach that someone who changed his mind cannot undo the first label, when that seems obvious.

steps.title: רב פפא: The change of mind happened within the short time window
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers why רבי יוסי had to rule on נמלך. The case is one where he changed his mind within תוך כדי דיבור. This makes the challenge against step 1 stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפא said: We are talking about someone who changed his mind within the time it takes to say a short phrase.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question from step 4. רבי יוסי's ruling on נמלך is not obvious, because the person changed his mind very quickly, within תוך כדי דיבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי still says the animal is only an עולה substitute, even though the change came within תוך כדי דיבור. That means he does not count a quick addition as part of the first statement. This clashes with step 1, which said רבי יוסי holds that a quick addition does join the first statement.

keyTerms.meaning: He changed his mind
Within the short time it takes to say a brief phrase
We are speaking about

steps.confusionAlert: This line answers the question in step 4, but it also brings back the original challenge. If רבי יוסי ignores a change of mind made within תוך כדי דיבור, how can step 1 say he counts such additions as part of the first statement?

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said:
We are speaking of one who changed his mind within the time of a short phrase.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: נִמְלַךְ בְּתוֹךְ כְּדֵי דִיבּוּר קָאָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4. This completes the challenge against step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did רבי יוסי need to rule on נמלך?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is one where he changed his mind within תוך כדי דיבור, so the ruling is a real חידוש.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 1's claim that רבי יוסי holds תוך כדי דיבור counts as one statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי ignores a change of mind made within תוך כדי דיבור. So he does not seem to count such additions as part of the first statement.

steps.title: Two different lengths of the short time window
steps.stepSummary: There are two measures of תוך כדי דיבור. רבי יוסי rejects only the longer one, the time of a student's greeting. He accepts the shorter one, the time of a רב's greeting.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: There are two kinds of 'within the time of a short phrase.' One is the time it takes a student to greet his רב, and one is the time it takes the רב to greet his student. רבי יוסי does not accept the student's greeting, 'Peace upon you, my רבי and teacher,' because it is long. He does accept the רב's greeting, 'Peace upon you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting תוך כדי דיבור into a longer and a shorter measure. רבי יוסי accepts only the shorter one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the נמלך case, the change of mind came within the longer window, so רבי יוסי does not join it to the first statement. In step 1's case, the addition came within the shorter window, so it does join. Both statements of רבי יוסי now fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: A greeting (literally, 'asking after someone's peace')
'Peace upon you, my רבי and teacher': the student's longer greeting
Because it is longer
He does not hold of it / he does hold of it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי counts an addition as part of the first statement only within the short window, the time of a רב's greeting 'שלום עליך'. The longer window, the time of a student's greeting, is too long for him.

phrases.english: They say: There are two kinds of 'within the time of speech' –
one is the time of a student's greeting to his teacher,
and one is the time of the teacher's greeting to a student.
When does Rabbi Yosei not accept it?
Within the time of a student's greeting to his teacher:
'Peace upon you, my rabbi and teacher,' because that is long;
but within the time of the teacher's greeting to a student, 'Peace upon you' –
he does accept it.
phrases.notes: He means that within this shorter time, the added words join the first statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised by step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: two different measures of תוך כדי דיבור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is one measure of תוך כדי דיבור, so רבי יוסי's two rulings contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two measures. רבי יוסי rejects the longer one, a student's greeting, and accepts the shorter one, a רב's greeting.

steps.title: רבא: Witnesses contradicted first and later made זוממין are killed
steps.stepSummary: A new topic. רבא rules that witnesses who were first contradicted and later made זוממין still get the punishment of עדים זוממין. The reason is that הכחשה is the beginning of הזמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Witnesses who were contradicted and later were made זוממין are killed. The contradiction is the start of הזמה; it just was not finished yet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ruling of רבא about false witnesses. He says that being contradicted first does not save them from the punishment of זוממין later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that once their testimony was already knocked out by הכחשה, a later הזמה would not count. רבא says it does count, because הכחשה and הזמה are one process. הכחשה is the unfinished first stage, and הזמה finishes it.

keyTerms.meaning: Contradiction: other witnesses say the event did not happen as described
Other witnesses say the first witnesses were with them elsewhere at that time, which makes them עֵדִים זוֹמְמִין
They are killed, the punishment of זוממין in a capital case
It was completed

steps.confusionAlert: הכחשה and הזמה are not the same thing. Only הזמה brings the punishment of זוממין. רבא's point is that a הכחשה that came first does not block that punishment.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Witnesses who were contradicted
and in the end were made conspiring witnesses are killed.
For contradiction is the beginning of הזמה,
except that it was not completed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: עֵדִים שֶׁהוּכְחֲשׁוּ וּלְבַסּוֹף הוּזַּמּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the תוך כדי דיבור discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who were first contradicted and later made זוממין receive the punishment of זוממין, because הכחשה is the unfinished start of הזמה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the main rule that the rest of the סוגיא will try to prove and test.

steps.title: רבא's proof from witnesses about a slave's eye and tooth
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא as proof. Witnesses testify that a master blinded his slave's eye and then knocked out his tooth, which is what the master also says. They are then found to be זוממין, and they pay the slave the value of an eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How do I know this? Because a ברייתא teaches: Witnesses say, 'We testify about so-and-so that he blinded his slave's eye and then knocked out his tooth,' and this is what the master himself says. Then they are found to be זוממין. They pay the slave the value of an eye.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins proving his rule from a ברייתא about witnesses testifying on a master who injured his slave. Here the גמרא lays out the case; how it proves רבא's point is explained next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of injuries matters. A slave goes free for the first injury, so the master owes money only for the second one. The witnesses' version, eye first and then tooth, means the slave goes free and the master pays only for the tooth. The ברייתא's ruling that these witnesses, once found זוממין, pay the slave the value of an eye is puzzling on a simple reading. Steps 9 and 10 raise exactly this problem.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (introduces a proof)
We testify
That he blinded his slave's eye
The value of an eye
Witnesses proven false through הזמה

steps.confusionAlert: This step only lays out the case. Do not try to work out the proof yet; the גמרא explains how it supports רבא right after this.

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say this?
As it is taught: 'We testify about so-and-so
that he blinded his slave's eye
and knocked out his tooth' –
for that is what the master says;
phrases.notes: Here 'הרב' means the slave's master, not a teacher.

phrases.english: and they were found to be conspiring witnesses –
they pay the value of an eye to the slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רבא's rule in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that הכחשה followed by הזמה still brings the punishment of זוממין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא מכות): witnesses about a slave's eye and tooth, whose story the master also tells, are found זוממין and pay the slave the value of an eye.

steps.title: What case is the ברייתא describing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא is about. If there was only one set of witnesses besides the ones who made them זוממין, it makes no sense for them to pay the slave the value of his eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If it is just as the ברייתא says, with no other set of witnesses, why would the זוממין pay the slave for his eye? Their testimony set him free. Should they now also pay him for his eye?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what case the ברייתא is really talking about. It begins by testing the simple reading and finds a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the simple reading, the witnesses said the master blinded the eye first. That would set the slave free. If those witnesses were lying, their lie helped the slave, so it makes no sense to punish them by paying the slave.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What exactly are we talking about?
If you say (introduces a reading that is about to be rejected)
A set or group of witnesses
Freedom (a slave going free)

steps.confusionAlert: In the simple reading, the lying witnesses were trying to help the slave, not hurt him. That is why paying him makes no sense.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If we say it is just as it is taught,
that there is no other set of witnesses;
they pay the value of an eye to the slave?!
After they took him out to freedom,
must they pay the value of his eye?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what exact case lies behind the ברייתא רבא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the exact setup of witnesses in the ברייתא?
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of the ברייתא, with only one set of witnesses
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Witnesses whose lie would free the slave did not harm him, so they should not have to pay him.

steps.title: Two more problems with the simple reading
steps.stepSummary: There are two more problems with the simple reading. The lying witnesses should pay the master for the whole slave. Also, the master would not be pleased with testimony that frees his slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, they should have to pay the master the value of the whole slave! And also, the ברייתא says 'for the master says so.' Would the master really be happy with this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two more problems that show the simple reading cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If their testimony would free the slave, the person they tried to hurt is the master. So they should pay him for the whole slave. Also, the ברייתא's phrase 'the master says so' means the testimony suits the master, but no master is happy to lose his slave.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (adds another problem)
Here: the master of the slave
It suits him, he is pleased with it

phrases.english: And furthermore, the value of the whole slave
they should need to pay to the master!
And furthermore, "for the master says so" —
is the master pleased with this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, דְּמֵי כּוּלֵּיהּ עֶבֶד לְרַב בָּעֵי לְשַׁלּוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two more difficulties to the problem raised in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In that reading the master is the one harmed, so the payment should go to him, and he would not agree with the testimony.

steps.title: The real case: three sets of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must be about three sets of witnesses. The first set said tooth then eye, so the master owes the eye. The middle set said eye then tooth, so the master owes only the tooth. The first set contradicts the middle set.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't the case like this? Two witnesses came and said: 'He knocked out the tooth, then blinded the eye.' So the master must pay the slave for his eye. Then two middle witnesses came and said: 'The eye, and then the tooth.' So he only has to pay for the tooth. The first witnesses contradict the middle witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real case behind the ברייתא. It adds an earlier set of witnesses that the ברייתא does not mention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the tooth came first, the slave went free then, and the later eye injury was done to a free man, so the master owes the eye. The middle witnesses, the ones quoted in the ברייתא, would make the master pay only for the tooth, which hurts the slave. So when they are made זוממין, paying the slave makes sense. They were first contradicted and later made זוממין, which is exactly רבא's case.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it...? (offers the reading that must be correct)
The middle ones (the middle set of witnesses)
The first ones
They contradict

steps.whyThisMatters: This reading turns the ברייתא into a real proof for רבא. The middle witnesses were contradicted first and made זוממין later, and they still pay.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו כְּגוֹן דַּאֲתוֹ בֵּי תְרֵי,
phrases.english: Rather, is it not a case where two came

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי: ״הִפִּיל אֶת שִׁינּוֹ, סִימֵּא אֶת עֵינוֹ״ –
phrases.english: and said: "He knocked out his tooth, then blinded his eye" —

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָעֵי מֵיתִיב לֵיהּ הָרַב דְּמֵי עֵינוֹ;
phrases.english: so the master needs to give him the value of his eye;
and two middle witnesses came
phrases.notes: They're called 'middle' because the set that made them זוממין came after them. These are the witnesses quoted in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and said: "His eye, and then his tooth" —

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא בָּעֵי לְמִיתַּב לֵיהּ אֶלָּא דְּמֵי שִׁינּוֹ,
phrases.english: so he needs to give him only the value of his tooth,
and the first ones contradict the middle ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו כְּגוֹן דַּאֲתוֹ בֵּי תְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 and solves the problems raised in steps 9 and 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is about three sets of witnesses. The first set (tooth then eye) contradicts the middle set (eye then tooth), and the middle set is later made זוממין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (adding a set of witnesses the ברייתא does not mention)

steps.title: Why the master is pleased
steps.stepSummary: Now the phrase 'for the master says so' makes sense. The master is pleased with the middle witnesses, because they make him pay only for the tooth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what 'for the master says so' means: he is pleased with what the middle witnesses say.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes by showing how the ברייתא's wording fits the new case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle witnesses lower the master's payment from an eye to a tooth, so their testimony suits him. This solves the last problem from step 10. Steps 13 and 14 then finish רבא's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is (what the wording means)

steps.whatToRemember: In the ברייתא, the middle witnesses were first contradicted by an earlier set and only later made זוממין. They still pay the slave, which proves רבא's rule that הכחשה is the beginning of הזמה.

phrases.english: And this is "for the master says so" —
that he is pleased with what they say.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the case from step 11 to explain the wording that step 10 found difficult.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Read as a three-set case, every detail of the ברייתא fits, and it supports רבא: witnesses contradicted first and made זוממין later still pay.

steps.title: The middle witnesses are found to be lying and pay the slave
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on to say that the middle set of witnesses was found to be זוממין and pays the slave the value of an eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the ברייתא teaches: 'And they were found to be זוממין.' This means the middle set. 'They pay the value of an eye to the slave.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the next words of the ברייתא using the three-set picture from the last step. The middle witnesses, who had already been contradicted, are later shown to be זוממין and have to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle set testified 'eye, then tooth,' which would have cost the slave the payment for his eye. They were already contradicted by the first set, and only afterward were they made זוממין. Even so, the ברייתא says they still pay the slave. That is the key fact רבא needs for his proof.

keyTerms.meaning: And it teaches (the ברייתא goes on to say)
The middle ones (the middle set of witnesses)
They were found to be lying witnesses through הזמה
The value of an eye

phrases.english: And it teaches: "And they were found to be זוממין"
the middle ones,
"they pay the value of an eye to the slave."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the ברייתא with the three-set setup from steps 11-12 and reaches the line that matters for רבא's proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that witnesses who were already contradicted can still be made זוממין later.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: the middle set, already contradicted, is later found to be זוממין and pays the value of an eye to the slave.

steps.title: רבא's conclusion: contradiction is the start of הזמה
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא, רבא concludes that a הכחשה is the beginning of הזמה. Witnesses who were contradicted can still be made זוממין afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: a contradiction is the beginning of הזמה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא states what his proof shows. A contradiction does not end the story; the same witnesses can still be made זוממין later and have to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that once witnesses are contradicted, their testimony is simply cancelled, so there is nothing left to make זוממין. The ברייתא, as רבא reads it, shows the opposite. The middle set was contradicted first, then made זוממין, and they still paid.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (a proof's conclusion)
Contradiction: other witnesses say the event happened differently
Proving witnesses were not there at all, which makes them pay what they tried to cause
The beginning of

phrases.english: Learn from this:
contradiction is the beginning of הזמה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the legal rule out of the ברייתא line read in step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבא, witnesses who were contradicted can still later be made זוממין and pay. This conclusion is about to be challenged by אביי.

steps.title: אביי: the second set reversed the story and made them זוממין at the same time
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. The ברייתא can be about two sets of witnesses, where the second set both reversed the order of events and made the first set זוממין together.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: No. The case is where the second witnesses reversed the story and also made them זוממין.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes away רבא's proof by offering a different picture of the ברייתא. In his picture, there was no earlier contradiction that came before the הזמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא needed three sets so that a contradiction would happen first and the הזמה later. אביי says one second set did both at once: it said 'tooth, then eye' (the reverse order) and also said the first witnesses were not even there. Since the contradiction and the הזמה came together, the ברייתא proves nothing about whether a contradiction that came earlier is the beginning of הזמה.

keyTerms.meaning: No (rejecting the proof)
They reversed them (switched the order of eye and tooth)
They made them זוממין

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two pictures. רבא has three sets of witnesses, with the contradiction coming first. אביי has only two sets, with the contradiction and the הזמה coming at the same time.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא proves from the ברייתא that הכחשה is the beginning of הזמה. אביי rejects this by reading the ברייתא as a two-set case, where reversing the story and making the first set זוממין happened together.

phrases.english: Abaye said: No,
where they reversed them and made them זוממין.
phrases.notes: The second set said 'tooth, then eye,' and in the same testimony said the first set was not there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's conclusion from step 14 by redefining the case of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא, not necessarily רבא's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא does not have to involve three sets with an earlier contradiction. It can be two sets, where one set reverses the order and makes the first set זוממין at the same time, so no earlier contradiction exists.

steps.title: אביי asks how we know his reading is right
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks "From where?" He is getting ready to prove that the ברייתא is about two sets of witnesses, not three.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a short question, "From where?" This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing his proof that his reading of the ברייתא is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 15, אביי said the ברייתא could be about two sets of witnesses. In that reading, the second set both reversed the order of events and made the first set זוממין. Now he goes further: his reading is not just possible, it is the right one. He asks "from where?" so he can point to evidence in the ברייתא itself.

keyTerms.meaning: "From what?" or "From where?" A question asking for the source or proof of a claim.
A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה. Here it is the case of the slave's tooth and eye.

steps.confusionAlert: This "מִמַּאי" is not a challenge against אביי. It is אביי himself asking, to set up his own proof.

phrases.english: From where?
phrases.notes: אביי is the one asking: how do I know my two-witness reading of the ברייתא is right?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's rejection from Step 15. He moves from saying his reading is possible to getting ready to prove it is correct.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What in the ברייתא shows that it is about two sets of witnesses, where the second set both reversed the events and made the first set זוממין?
